then.text: You've my say-so already. Away to the first tee and give them a fright.

else.text: So the Starter sent you. Right. Three questions. Get them right and you've my say-so. Get them wrong and go and read the plaques on the course like everybody else.
Which hole is the Road Hole?

then.text: What crosses the Swilcan Burn on the 1st and 18th?
Spot on, all three. You've been reading. Tell the Starter Old Tam says you'll do.

else.text: No. Away and look at the plaque by the big bunker, then come back.
No. The plaque by the burn will put you right.
No. Seventeen is the Road Hole. Go and read the plaque by its bunker and come back.

In here you'll see featheries: leather balls stuffed with boiled goose feathers. A good ball maker managed a few a day. Then in the 1840s came the gutty, made of gutta-percha, and everybody could afford to lose a ball.
And the old clubs had names, not numbers: the niblick, the mashie, the cleek, the spoon. A spoon! Imagine telling your mother you're off out with your spoon.
